notes: The ship's floor plan inside its hull: the outside's plan (the owner's plan v7, built at 46 m on PRD #10) split into the rooms, the walkway and what is left out, the inside step of the owner's loop of 2026-10-19. Read by tools/props/scene/ship_floor.py, which measures every room's size and section from the hull itself (`hull`, plan v7's hull at 46 m, carried here since its own file, data/definitions/ship.json, was retired on 2026-10-21), so no size here can drift from the hull.
Frame as the ship plan's, built metres: y back from the nose spike's tip, x across (starboard positive, the side ring's side), z up from the ground the ship stands on.

People keep their size at 46 m: doors stay 0.9 x 2.0 m and rooms take a person's ceiling; only the hull's lengths grow. The fix-ship-rooms branch scaled every room 1.5 times instead (ceilings 3 to 5 m, a 1.8 m walkway): replaced by this plan.

Sizes and order come from the hull and the story: the cockpit under the nose windows, the navigation module behind it in the same room, the crew's quarters and galley together, storage beside the ship's lock so cargo comes in through the one hatch, the engine room aft over the engines, the walkway joining them all.
made: 2026-10-19, the ship lead, from plan v7 at 46 m; navigation merged into the cockpit (the owner, 2026-10-21, on the hangar's plan: "changed cockpit to cockpit and nav ; and removed nav"; from tail to nose the engine room, shiplock (west) and galley (east), storage (west) and quarters (east), the walkway down the middle, at the nose one room 'cockpit and nav'; rooms fill the hull width); the room runs from the side rooms to the nose, the cockpit at the nose and a navigation module in its middle (the owner, 2026-10-21 (about 15:30, on the hangar plan where he had dragged the cockpit to the nose, leaving a gap behind it): "this, should still be cockpit, there and nav in the middle, like actual nav module, but in the same room")
deck_why: the main deck's floor over the ground: plan v7's 1.6 m drawn times 1.5, the height the hull's side ring is built on (fix-ship-hull)
lining_why: the hull's frame and lining between its outside and a room's wall
floor_depth_why: the deck's structure under a floor: the hull's keel must lie at least this far under it
head_why: a person's height over a floor: a room is as wide as the hull is at its floor and at this height, the narrower
ceiling_why: a room's clear height on the one deck; the hull's space over it (2.0 to 2.9 m clear from y 22 to 34) is the service space

walkway.for: the corridor joining every room, cockpit to engine room, down the ship's middle line
holds: grey panelled walls and ceiling, dark deck, a steel grating down the middle of the deck
steel frame ribs arching over the corridor between the doors
white light strips down the ceiling, amber strips along the wall tops
the rooms' doors in hexagonal orange and white frames off both sides, the cockpit and nav's door at its forward end

rooms.name: cockpit and nav
rooms.for: flying and navigating the ship, one room: the cockpit at the nose, two pilot seats and consoles under the nose windows; the navigation module in its middle, a star map table with its consoles
rooms.why: one room from the side rooms forward to the nose: as far forward as a person still stands (2.2 m clear at 9.7 m; ahead of it the nose bay), as wide as the hull; its roof at the nose is the windows, so its ceiling is the hull's up to 3.9 m, flat at 3.9 m behind them; the cockpit at the nose end, the navigation module in the middle, the aft door to the walkway (the owner, 2026-10-21 (about 15:30, on the hangar plan where he had dragged the cockpit to the nose, leaving a gap behind it): "this, should still be cockpit, there and nav in the middle, like actual nav module, but in the same room"; earlier: "changed cockpit to cockpit and nav ; and removed nav")
holds: at the nose end, the cockpit: two chunky dark padded pilot seats side by side, facing the windows, a flight stick for each
the throttle pedestal between the seats, levers and switch rows on its top
the main console across the front: three screens, the middle red-orange, two amber, a thrust indicator between them, a cyan light bar along its top
angled side consoles with screens and red-lit switches, and equipment racks filling the room's wide sides
the windows in the sloping roof over the seats, split by frame ribs, two cyan light panels at their top
the overhead console with two black vent boxes, black equipment boxes in the ceiling's corners
in the room's middle, the navigation module: a star map table glowing amber with a cyan route, its consoles round it with a seat before each
two screens hung over the star map table: the route between the Moon and Mars
warm amber light strips along the ceiling's edges and the wall tops, small orange lamps in the upper front corners, a white strip and a vent in the ceiling behind the windows
dark grey panelled walls and ceiling, dark deck with a grated step between the seats
the aft door to the walkway in the ship's hexagonal frame

rooms.for: sleep: four bunks in two stacks (orange padded), lockers; save and skip time
rooms.why: the crew's rooms together on the port side, away from the hatch; 6 m holds the two bunk stacks and the lockers
holds: four bunks in two stacks with thick orange padded mattresses on dark frames
lockers for the crew's kit
dark grey wall desks with switch rows under wall screens with amber and white readouts, one a round glowing display
white light strips along the ceiling and the wall tops, black ceiling boxes and vents
grey panelled walls and ceiling, dark deck plates with lit inlays

rooms.name: storage
rooms.for: storage: cargo racks and crates for the base's supplies and parts
rooms.why: beside the ship's lock, so cargo comes in through the one hatch and goes straight to the racks; forward to the cockpit and nav now navigation is merged (the owner, 2026-10-21, on the hangar's plan: "changed cockpit to cockpit and nav ; and removed nav"; from tail to nose the engine room, shiplock (west) and galley (east), storage (west) and quarters (east), the walkway down the middle, at the nose one room 'cockpit and nav'; rooms fill the hull width)
holds: tall cargo racks with strapped supplies along the hull wall and the back wall
crates of the base's supplies and parts on the deck
equipment boxes and a vent in the ceiling
amber light strips at the wall tops, a white strip in the ceiling
grey panelled walls and ceiling, dark deck

rooms.why: beside the quarters; 6 m holds the counter along the hull and the table
holds: a counter along the hull wall with a cooker, a sink and cupboards
food stores beside the counter
a table with fold-down seats round it
a wall screen on the back wall
amber light strips at the wall tops, white strips and vents in the ceiling
grey panelled walls and ceiling, dark deck

rooms.name: ship's lock
rooms.for: the one way in and out, and the dock: the side ring's round hatch in its hull wall, the inner door onto the walkway, lockers for the suits
rooms.why: behind the side ring (the docking hatch and the people airlock in one opening, PRD #10, 2026-10-18), which stands at 28.64 m on the starboard side

suit lockers along the back wall
the cycle panel by the outer hatch and two orange lamps

holds: the power core: an upright cylinder with amber-lit rings
fuel tanks against the walls of the narrow stern bay at the back, between the two main engines
engine consoles with screens along the starboard wall
pipes from the core and tanks into the stern bay, cables over the ceiling
junction boxes and a toolbox for repairs
orange lamps, amber strips, white ceiling strips; equipment boxes and vents in the ceiling

left_out.why: ahead of the cockpit the hull is under 2.2 m over the deck and narrows to the spike: sensors and the nose thrusters, no room
between the deck and the keel (0.3 to 1.3 m): the landing legs, the lift thrusters and the tanks' pipes, no room
over the rooms' ceilings, 2.0 to 2.9 m clear from y 22 to 34: ducts and cables; a second deck of a person's height would fit only from about y 28 to 31 (see the questions)
the stern block narrows and its keel rises past a floor: the main engines' backs, no room

questions.ask: the way in: the side ring (PRD #10, 2026-10-18: the docking hatch and the people airlock in one opening) or the stern block's hatch (plan v7, 2026-10-14: the dark block at the stern is the airlock)?
questions.ours: the side ring only, one opening as the later call says; the stern block becomes the engine room's aft bay and has no hatch

questions.ask: one deck or two: the 46 m hull has 2.0 to 2.9 m clear over a 2.6 m ceiling between y 22 and 34, a person-high second deck only from about y 28 to 31
questions.ours: one deck, as the owner's one-deck cutaway reference; the space over it is service space

questions.ask: the cockpit is as wide as the hull under the windows, 7.9 to 9.1 m
questions.ours: keep it: the consoles and the overhead panels fill its sides, the two seats in the middle

hull.from: the owner's plan v7 hull (data/definitions/ship.json, drawn at 31 m) built at the floor plan's 46 m by tools/props/library/inside/ship_outline.py, written here on 2026-10-21 when ship.json was retired, so the floor plan carries its own hull
hull.stations_are: front to back, every 0.25 drawn metres: y back from the nose spike's tip, half the body's width at its waist, its keel and top over the ground, built metres
hull.section_is: a station's corners from the keel up, as (share of its half width, share of its height from the keel): a flat keel, a lower chine, the waist, an upper chine and a flat deck

drawn.is: plan v7 as drawn: its length and each of its rooms' length along the ship, drawn metres
